# Ecological detection data, in one format

<p class="lead">
Occupancy surveys, repeated counts, capture histories and community
detection matrices share a structure: a unit carries a latent state that is
observed imperfectly across repeated probes. **eco** asks whether the
<a href="https://itemresponsewarehouse.org">Item Response Warehouse</a>'s
one-long-table approach works for that structure, and builds real tables to
find out.
</p>
:::

## The idea in one table

Every table has the IRW's three-column core under local names, plus two time
indices that ecologists will recognise as primary and secondary sampling
periods.

| Column | What it holds | IRW name |
|---|---|---|
| `unit` | the thing carrying the latent state: a site, camera, transect, or an individual animal | `id` |
| `taxon` | the species probed for, even when there is only one | `item` |
| `y` | the observation: 0/1 detection, a count, or a coded state | `resp` |
| `period` | primary period, across which the latent state may change | occasion column |
| `occasion` | replicate survey within a period, across which closure is assumed | occasion column |

Covariates are prefixed by the level at which they are constant (`unit_`,
`period_` for unit by period, `obs_` for the survey row, `taxon_` for the
species), which is exactly the three-level split that `unmarked`,
`spOccupancy` and the AHM BUGS code expect. A row exists if and only if a
survey happened; a missing row is never a zero. A one-line rename gives the
IRW view, and that view validates under IRW v1.0 unchanged.

## Where things stand

The work ran in four passes.

1. A [standard](standard.html) was drafted against IRW v1.0 and the data
   structures of `unmarked`, `marked`, `spOccupancy` and the AHM code.
2. Six datasets bundled with R packages were converted to it and back, with
   identical arrays and identical model estimates on either side.
3. Six real deposits from Dryad, Zenodo, Dataverse and ScienceBase were run
   through an IRW-style pipeline, to see the standard meet messy data. The
   open design decisions were then ruled on and the standard frozen as
   v1.0-draft; the [about](about.html) page records each ruling.
4. The pipeline was run as a pipeline: a validator that cites clauses, CI
   that runs it on every change, a metadata layer the site and the R package
   read, and a release ledger. Five further batches took the corpus to
   `r s$n_tables` tables across `r s$n_families` model families, including the
   first spatial capture-recapture, distance-sampling, double-observer and
   eDNA multi-scale tables, each of which stretches the format in a declared
   way.

Every table passes both validators. `r s$n_below_floor` of the `r s$n_tables`
are below the sample floor and say so; `r s$n_experimental` are tagged
experimental and may be restructured between versions. What is not yet done:
the queue holds more inspected candidates than have been built, citations and
per-table landing pages are planned but not built, and nothing has been
fitted across the corpus beyond the [first look](firstlook.html).

*Tables last built `r s$built`.*
